reason: The full batch, approved T10 design, supplier claims and proofs, and affected consumers were reviewed. Request one local repair round for the scope and page-local defects below; no owner escalation is needed at this stage.

findings.reason: The Definition makes a finite rational expression certificate and rational initial/reset state mandatory. The approved T10 contract permits explicitly supplied valid C1 dense/error data generally and specifies the rational residual checker as one sufficient provider branch. Expand the interface to admit a justified general provider while retaining the rational branch, then update consumers that currently rely on the rational-only error proof.

The supplier root isolator requires a finite dyadic initial interval, but the algorithm admits any positive-length trial interval. Also, its width target only limits unresolved boxes; a unique-root result may be wider, and the stated refinement branch has no executable instructions or clearly aggregated box budget. Specify compatible interval inputs, a finite endpoint-safe refinement procedure charged to B_root, and the certificate needed to apply priority to an exactly simultaneous tie; otherwise return inconclusive.

The roots 1/4 and 3/4 lie on the smooth isolator's deterministic bisection boundaries. Its derivative test on the parent intervals can fail, leaving endpoint roots unresolved in the child boxes; the proof therefore does not establish that complete isolation finds both roots. Use roots away from those boundaries, such as 1/3 and 2/3, or provide an exact endpoint-root isolation route.

The page says event absence is concluded only when the whole step is root-free. The algorithm also accepts a no-event step when complete isolation finds roots but certifies each as oppositely oriented. Rephrase the summary to match the actual enabled-event rule.

F1 paraphrases the system definition as though every guard zero were an event, although the definition requires an oriented crossing. This example uses a grazing root, which is not an enabled event under that definition. Clarify that it demonstrates root-location sensitivity at a guard contact.

The example omits a fixed total priority, so as written it is not a system satisfying the linked definition. Identify it as an incomplete specification and compare the resulting continuations under explicit priority orders.

consumer_checks.reason: Generalize its certificate premise to the valid supplied C1 error and guard bounds while preserving the proved event-time inequality.
Update its provider interface and make root-box refinement, interval admissibility, budget accounting, and tie evidence executable.
Its current facts derive local error from the rational residual checker; state the general certified local-error premise so the theorem supports the approved provider interface.
Its proof currently uses the rational checker for local error and must be checked against the generalized provider contract and revised algorithm.
Adjust the example or its isolation evidence to match the actual root isolator behavior at bisection-boundary roots.
Clarify that the grazing zero is a guard contact, not an enabled event under the linked definition.
Make explicit that the example compares completions of a specification without a priority rule.
Align its no-event summary with the algorithm's handling of oppositely oriented roots.
Its explicit dense-error, transversality, residual, reset, and field bounds support the stated local estimates.
The external consumer supplies its own explicit general C1 error and guard certificates and uses the unchanged transverse-time and reset bounds consistently.
